judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is a carousel image in 'Conheça nossas novas exposições' with alt="Passados-imaginados.jpg", the exact file name in its src. In the Chromium accessibility tree it is exposed as an image named from the alt (not ignored, no aria-hidden, not inside a link or a named ancestor), and the live page's server HTML still has the same alt. I opened the image file: it is a photograph, showing visitors around a city model, with questions projected on the walls, not a picture of the words in the file name. The alt is the exhibition title from the visible caption (PASSADOS IMAGINADOS) with file-name residue (hyphens and .jpg), so it does not describe the image, and the image is not marked as decorative either (alt is not empty). F30 names file names that are not valid alternatives in their own right, ACT rule 9eb3f6 fails a file name with its extension even when the stem matches the subject, and F39 fails a non-null alt on an image that should be ignored, so the image fails whether it is informative or decorative. The image being off-screen at capture time (the widget is an infinite marquee) does not matter: it scrolls into view and screen readers read it anyway. I found no technique that makes it pass.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the header logo, the only content of the link to the home page. Its alt 'logo-museu' is the file name logo-museu.png without the extension. The crop and the screenshot show a picture of the words 'MUSEU DO IPIRANGA — USP'. In the Chromium accessibility tree, the link is named 'logo-museu' from its contents. The site-title link 'Museu do Ipiranga' (p.main-title.bhf-hidden) is display:none and not in the tree, and the live markup has no aria-label or title on the link. 'logo-museu' ('museum logo') leaves out the museum's name and the USP text, and it does not say where the link goes, so it does not serve the same purpose (F30). The finding's claim (a file name or placeholder) holds. The same name also weakens link purpose (2.4.4).

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the footer newsletter's 'Digite seu Nome' field, injected by the iSend widget: input type=text name=name, named only by its placeholder, with no autocomplete attribute and no form element around it. It asks for the visitor's own name, a purpose in the 1.3.5 list ('name'). The Understanding document says heuristics such as the name attribute are not enough: the purpose must be exposed through the autocomplete attribute (H98). The snapshot records Chromium's FormInputAssignedAutocompleteValueToIdOrNameAttributeError issue on this field, which confirms the side claim. The live iSend script creates its inputs without ever setting autocomplete, so the field still fails today. Whether the right token is name or given-name, no purpose is identified.
